process: L26-002-59Elm8myGEc

- Guessing the reaction to NFP is gambling; being right on direction still gets you hurt by volatility and slippage ([0:04:14](https://youtu.be/59Elm8myGEc?t=254), [0:35:34](https://youtu.be/59Elm8myGEc?t=2134)).
- Impatient new traders chase quick runs; if they win one they re-enter the same day and give it back ([0:09:54](https://youtu.be/59Elm8myGEc?t=594)).
- Don't fall in love with unrealized profit; bank partials ([0:18:41](https://youtu.be/59Elm8myGEc?t=1121)).
- Study price action, not signal services or indicators; he lost money to those as a young trader ([0:09:05](https://youtu.be/59Elm8myGEc?t=545)).
- Backtest and journal daily for weeks; annotate the chart ([0:29:06](https://youtu.be/59Elm8myGEc?t=1746)).
- Stand aside if you cannot see what is likely to occur ([0:39:32](https://youtu.be/59Elm8myGEc?t=2372)).
- Several off-topic digressions (criticism from detractors, crude nightclub analogy) carry only the "be where the crowd isn't" message.
L26-003-kRShZKZlvJ4

- Use prop-firm "lockout" features: lock yourself out of trading the rest of NFP week (Wed-Fri) if you are new, inexperienced, impulsive or prone to tilt; the Thursday/Friday price action is detrimental to people with low self-control. Experienced non-impulsive traders can ignore this ([0:11:28](https://youtu.be/kRShZKZlvJ4?t=688), [0:12:15](https://youtu.be/kRShZKZlvJ4?t=735)).
- He did not add to the winner because he was not "inspired" and was already taking partials ([0:08:17](https://youtu.be/kRShZKZlvJ4?t=497)).
- Posting predictions publicly ahead of time (the Twitter quiz) as a drill.
- Closing monologue: time goes fast; do not spend time on needless things ([0:13:03](https://youtu.be/kRShZKZlvJ4?t=783)).

- **Execution discipline:** Show live execution, not market replay, to prove the concept works without hindsight bias. Execution management proves it's not fake.
- **Accepting stop-outs:** If stopped out after following rules, that's okay. Rules protect you over time. Proper risk framing (3 defensive levels) shows how much damage was avoided.
- **Staggering profits:** "Give myself a steak dinner" (remove risk/lock profit) early rather than betting everything on final target.
- **Patience on pullbacks:** Don't panic when price retraces to support (CE, order block, etc.); give it a chance to respond.
- **Tape reading:** No special tools required; simple candlestick order flow (bodies, wicks, volume gaps) is sufficient.
- **Risk per trade:** Example given: 12 cars (12 contracts) risking $525 for potential $3,000 return = good risk/reward.
- **Timestamps for psychology:** [0:15:16](https://youtu.be/7M56e9O06Ko?t=916) "don't be afraid," [0:21:31](https://youtu.be/7M56e9O06Ko?t=1291) explains market replay criticism and proves execution over hypothetical trade.
L26-005-I7fIf1eEz0w

- **Patience on revisits:** "It may not get there the first time it reaches for it. Then it pulls it all the way back down" — allow time for price to return to key levels.
- **Multiple timeframes:** Review on multiple chart scales (daily, 4h, 1h, 30m, etc.) to identify session boundaries and key zones.
- **Live vs. commentary:** ICT acknowledges this is post-market commentary, not live; value is in understanding the logic, not timing entries.
- **Timestamps for psychology:** [0:06:42](https://youtu.be/I7fIf1eEz0w?t=402) "watch this candlestick right there" — teach observation; [0:07:30](https://youtu.be/I7fIf1eEz0w?t=450) "I'd like to see it extrapolate up into" — express intention without forcing it.
L26-006-UVVmS0de0g0

- **Stalking, not chasing:** "I'm not reacting. I'm waiting. I'm anticipating. I'm expecting. I am stalking, hunting, pursuing."
- **Pre-market prep:** ICT did a pre-market scalp (9:30–10:00 AM window) for $6,990 to prove macros work.
- **Scaling out:** When order flow signals exhaustion (bodies failing to reach expected target, not closing above key level), exit partial or full.
- **Precision vs. volume:** No special tools needed; just candlestick open, high, low, close + time.
- **Daily chart as foundation:** All intraday levels anchor to daily chart structure (high, low, wick CE).
- **Addressing critics:** Students who claim "macros don't exist" or "it doesn't work" simply don't know the full ruleset; automation efforts fail because rules are incomplete.
- **Timestamps for psychology:** [0:39:55](https://youtu.be/UVVmS0de0g0?t=2395) "I promise you, if you listen to me... you will know more about how price and why price and when price will do things," [0:50:19](https://youtu.be/UVVmS0de0g0?t=3019) "I promise you that will never happen because this isn't even my best stuff."
L26-009-50VbES10ULs

- **Pre-market planning:** ICT noted at 9:21 AM (pre-RTH) that large range expansion was incoming based on daily chart inside days, not just FOMC calendar.
- **Caution on uncertainty:** First FOMC with new Fed chair warranted earlier partial exits (not holding for full target).
- **Taking profit:** Closed initial partial as market broke lower; allowed stop-losses to be hit on remaining contracts, then re-entered near daily lows.
- **Recording challenges:** ICT notes technical issues with screen recording (Alt+R Windows tool) when trading outside recording window; transparency about trade closure confirms execution (not Photoshop).
- **Dealing with skepticism:** $33,800 profit proves the methodology regardless of critics' concerns about record-keeping.
- **Timestamps for psychology:** [0:09:08](https://youtu.be/50VbES10ULs?t=548) "I was more inclined to take off partials," [0:12:24](https://youtu.be/50VbES10ULs?t=744) "I wanted to take some profit right there."

- [0:05:01](https://youtu.be/xnbtp_j81lI?t=301) — repetition builds subconscious pattern reading so you can read the tape live.

- [0:23:59](https://youtu.be/xnbtp_j81lI?t=1439) — record losing days as what you should have done; no dollar-loss entries.

L26-011-9W4YpyAg5RY

- **Teaching through execution:** ICT trades with 1 contract (vs. usual 6) after a holiday to demonstrate the concept while protecting capital. This shows students the risk discipline required for uncertain conditions.
- **Independence and effort:** "You do not need to know all these things, but if you want to know what I'm dealing with when I'm acting on it, this is what you get." Students must do their own due diligence; no hand-holding.
- **Handling criticism:** ICT explicitly warns against commenting "it's too complicated" — such comments indicate lack of teachability. He mutes/hides such comments.
- **Simplicity is insufficient:** ICT addresses the myth that simple trading rules work; they don't. Superior trading requires complexity and mastery.
- **Post-holiday caution:** "We don't want to go in with heavy leverage. We don't want to go in thinking you know everything. We don't want to go in demanding the best of the best in exits."
- **Timestamps for psychology:** [0:11:19](https://youtu.be/9W4YpyAg5RY?t=679) "if you want to know what I'm dealing with," [0:14:29](https://youtu.be/9W4YpyAg5RY?t=869) "I know all your stuff," [0:20:06](https://youtu.be/9W4YpyAg5RY?t=1206) "Because you didn't listen to the video," [0:29:00](https://youtu.be/9W4YpyAg5RY?t=1740) "low-hanging fruit is... a protocol to prevent you from being greedy."
L26-012-VBgfJRMVCaI

- [0:03:31](https://youtu.be/VBgfJRMVCaI?t=211) / [0:04:23](https://youtu.be/VBgfJRMVCaI?t=263) — aligning with price: "either I'm offside or onside with my initial expectation."
- [0:07:44](https://youtu.be/VBgfJRMVCaI?t=464) — after holidays, let the market work out its "funk or apprehension or excitement or laziness"; he just wants a pulse.
- [0:10:29](https://youtu.be/VBgfJRMVCaI?t=629) — pay yourself on new lows; don't demand the full target while developing your model.
- [0:15:30](https://youtu.be/VBgfJRMVCaI?t=930) — "it's not about the money. It's about you getting in sync with price action." Don't try to force a will.
- Also repeats "Never market replay" in passing at [0:05:20](https://youtu.be/VBgfJRMVCaI?t=320).

- Predict, do not react ([0:24:10](https://youtu.be/-Qag-99u_BM?t=1450)): reacting means you do not know when something will happen, which is fear of missing the setup. He says he has no fear of missing a trade because price is scripted.
- He will not put students into live trades to copy ([0:24:57](https://youtu.be/-Qag-99u_BM?t=1497)): he wants independent traders, not followers, and tells students to learn what they need and move on.
- Study, do not rush ([0:58:08](https://youtu.be/-Qag-99u_BM?t=3488)): you cannot speed up the process; demanding success by a deadline only lengthens it. Let experience come organically.
- Keep a record of what he teaches versus how the market delivers ([0:57:19](https://youtu.be/-Qag-99u_BM?t=3439)); ask the right questions, such as why critics never address his calls made before the fact.
- Trading real money is never advised by him; he stresses that his content is free and not trade signals ([0:29:44](https://youtu.be/-Qag-99u_BM?t=1784)).
- Long non-technical stretch from about 0:26 to 0:57: reputation, critics, faith and life advice, motivation beyond money (not trading content). The only trading-relevant theme is his closing view that how you behave and manage money matters as much as winning, because losing a large account is hard to recover from ([0:49:13](https://youtu.be/-Qag-99u_BM?t=2953)).
L26-014-L81eMQhmXmc

- Do not rush; trying to learn everything fast means learning nothing ([0:01:58](https://youtu.be/L81eMQhmXmc?t=118)).
- Predict, do not react: recording price action daily builds the ability to anticipate it ([0:06:53](https://youtu.be/L81eMQhmXmc?t=413)); if you cannot stick to a three-screenshot routine, you cannot follow a trading model.
- Pattern recognition through repetition: seeing the same thing daily in slightly different forms builds experience he cannot give you, and removes the urge to chase or system-hop ([0:21:33](https://youtu.be/L81eMQhmXmc?t=1293), [0:22:22](https://youtu.be/L81eMQhmXmc?t=1342)).
- Everything here is time-based, so it transposes to any session or time frame, even if you plan to trade London, Asia or the afternoon ([0:23:09](https://youtu.be/L81eMQhmXmc?t=1389)).
- Do not "Netflix and chill" through videos; the work of logging is where the benefit is ([0:25:34](https://youtu.be/L81eMQhmXmc?t=1534)).
- Journal habit: he logs by hand, writing numbers and times; write observations on the chart itself, treat as your business ([0:27:09](https://youtu.be/L81eMQhmXmc?t=1629)).
L26-015-Khj1veL49r8

- Lock in profit in steps but do not move the stop so soon that a stop-hunt pop takes you out ([0:12:54](https://youtu.be/Khj1veL49r8?t=774)).
- Accept risking open profit to get the full move ("you want 10 grand, you got to risk being stopped out") but do not give back more than about 5,000 unrealized ([0:20:09](https://youtu.be/Khj1veL49r8?t=1209)).
- Close manually when the idea is no longer wanted even if the target might still hit ([0:22:23](https://youtu.be/Khj1veL49r8?t=1343)).
- Think like the market maker: ask why stops would be left alone ([0:12:54](https://youtu.be/Khj1veL49r8?t=774)).
- Live execution rather than market replay is stressed repeatedly ([0:08:09](https://youtu.be/Khj1veL49r8?t=489), [0:13:42](https://youtu.be/Khj1veL49r8?t=822)).
- Banter content (Deadpool technique, "Crayola model", jokes about critics and heat maps) carries no rule; the Deadpool joke is a gag about dragging the live candle.
L26-016-xpH0wDANtmM

- **Early profit-taking on NFP week:** ICT took 2 contracts off early (partial exit at half the gap FPFVG) despite potential for larger move, to lock profit due to NFP week risk.
- **Patience on second stage:** "I'm just allowing the market to find its legs to go lower" — don't force; let the redistribution phase play out.
- **Stop placement based on stages:** Stop is anchored to stage 1 distribution boundary; don't chase it lower during stage 2 aggressive sell-off.
- **Dealing with retracements:** Understanding what stage the market is in allows you to hold through retracements that would scare weak traders.
- **Addressing critics:** "Either be doing better than I am with accuracy and precision or just keep your opinion to yourself." No tolerance for hindsight criticism.
- **Timestamps for psychology:** [0:05:17](https://youtu.be/xpH0wDANtmM?t=317) "I don't want to build it any larger than that," [0:20:07](https://youtu.be/xpH0wDANtmM?t=1207) "I'm allowing the market to breathe," [0:23:30](https://youtu.be/xpH0wDANtmM?t=1410) "you can't capture the full range unless you risk the trade holding for the full range."

- [0:14:56](https://youtu.be/MB7clEZvF7s?t=896) — information management takes little work; laziness and refusing to follow rules is the real cause of failure (his claim after 34 years of students).
- [0:23:09](https://youtu.be/MB7clEZvF7s?t=1389) — if this much is "too complicated," he says it won't work for you.
- [0:28:42](https://youtu.be/MB7clEZvF7s?t=1722) — he has never promised profitability; he offers a way to read price action and a methodology.
- [0:40:00](https://youtu.be/MB7clEZvF7s?t=2400) — beginners want to buy FVGs/breakers/models; all of that is easier when the matrix info is on the chart.
- [0:44:54](https://youtu.be/MB7clEZvF7s?t=2694) / [0:45:41](https://youtu.be/MB7clEZvF7s?t=2741) — key PD arrays tell you "when I should be participating and when I should just sit still"; a new student should abstain in no-man's land after 11:00 a.m. in non-farm payroll week; chasing real money before knowing what you're doing leads to hardship.

L26-018-djabvhihIM8

- "Pantomiming a new student": the first two months should be tape reading and journaling, not demo trading. Say the hypothetical entry, stop and partial aloud and write them down ([0:32:18](https://youtu.be/djabvhihIM8?t=1938): "Just watching ain't enough", keep a notepad; [1:13:46](https://youtu.be/djabvhihIM8?t=4426)).
- Do not worry about pretend money; the value is reading price action around the specific levels taught in the lectures ([1:03:17](https://youtu.be/djabvhihIM8?t=3797)).
- Be forgiving of yourself when chopped up; experience the chop while only observing, so you learn the cost of chasing ([0:31:27](https://youtu.be/djabvhihIM8?t=1887)).
- Don't be upset about a stop-out after a partial banked 20 handles; being upset is "foolish especially if you're brand new" ([1:00:07](https://youtu.be/djabvhihIM8?t=3607)).
- Accept being wrong sometimes ("I could be wrong still. It happens") and having a losing transaction; he wants students to see a loser in the day ([1:17:29](https://youtu.be/djabvhihIM8?t=4649)).
- Jokes: the "dead pull technique" (mentally "pulling" price up) is a joke about wishful thinking, not a technique ([0:20:37](https://youtu.be/djabvhihIM8?t=1237)).
- Slow, long videos are justified: explaining two hours of price action on a candle-by-candle basis cannot be said in fewer words.
L26-019-BWEPtHZ1Y2Y

- Patience and discipline early; early habits stick; being wrong at first is normal and should not push you out.
- You are not aiming to be right; aim for consistently following a model and measure its probabilities yourself ([1:12:25](https://youtu.be/BWEPtHZ1Y2Y?t=4345)).
- Probable setups require knowing why price should go there; mistakes are the operator's own errors ([0:57:32](https://youtu.be/BWEPtHZ1Y2Y?t=3452)).
- Take a partial to pay yourself; manage the stop to avoid fear-based holding ([1:30:26](https://youtu.be/BWEPtHZ1Y2Y?t=5426)).
- Risk: if your size makes a stop too big, drop to micros; if you can't accept micro profits you are gambling ([1:57:44](https://youtu.be/BWEPtHZ1Y2Y?t=7064)).
- Secondary income is a skill that takes time; not promised to everyone ([1:27:54](https://youtu.be/BWEPtHZ1Y2Y?t=5274)).
- Journal the observation points and annotate them yourself.
L26-020-iSWZOe3aUFE

- **Partial exit on event days:** ICT took profits around Fed chair speech (10 AM) due to anticipated volatility spike; this is prudent risk management on Jackson Hole days.
- **Recording technical issues:** Camtasia rendering limitations prevented recording full trade opening; ICT showed entries in screenshot but acknowledged the gap transparently.
- **Acceptance of imperfection:** "I didn't do it perfectly here" — even ICT doesn't execute perfectly on event-driven days; the process matters more than perfection.
- **Learning from losses, not dwelling:** When you take a loss, analyze what went wrong, take notes, improve. Don't spiral into self-doubt or toxicity.
- **Persona vs. reality:** Separate "ICT the content creator" from "the actual trading methodology." The persona attracts attention; the methodology is what works. Study the methodology, not the personality.

Cuz I'm going to bring your audience right to center stage," [0:19:02](https://youtu.be/iSWZOe3aUFE?t=1142) "once you're here, you're getting the real person, me."
L26-021-MD1Ts09dkYs

- Prediction not reaction: "We're not reacting. We're predicting. Every trader is predicting whether they want to admit it" ([0:26:05](https://youtu.be/MD1Ts09dkYs?t=1565)); anticipating is how you avoid emotional reactions to unrealized profit or fear.
- Over-leverage, overtrading and entering before you should wreck even a good model: "Even if they have a winning system, you'll lose because you're the person that's going to wreck it" ([0:25:16](https://youtu.be/MD1Ts09dkYs?t=1516)).
- He says his stop management lets him sit within one tick of the stop because he knows the structure; stops placed where price "never goes".
- He will never trade live so others can copy: if everyone wants the same fill nobody gets it; "I'm not going to dilute my efficiency" ([0:32:31](https://youtu.be/MD1Ts09dkYs?t=1951)–[0:34:05](https://youtu.be/MD1Ts09dkYs?t=2045)).
- Learn his language so the cursor is not necessary; his speech is more important than the cursor in fast markets ([0:13:14](https://youtu.be/MD1Ts09dkYs?t=794)).
- Slow down; go back through your own charts, annotate and log for backtesting; next week he will take his son Kaden through Monday-Friday daily on what to look for, log and annotate ([0:40:02](https://youtu.be/MD1Ts09dkYs?t=2402)).
- A live trade has real risk; hypothetical position boxes are not a trade; market replay cannot reproduce live fills ([0:35:40](https://youtu.be/MD1Ts09dkYs?t=2140), [0:41:40](https://youtu.be/MD1Ts09dkYs?t=2500)).
- Scalping the sell-off is fine, but it is a different style from day-trading with position in mind ([0:09:58](https://youtu.be/MD1Ts09dkYs?t=598)).
L26-022-SUcRywSry5U

- **Precision stop placement:** "Stop loss game is best in the business" — ICT's stop placements are within single ticks of the intended level, demonstrating mastery.
- **Patience through cork pattern:** Consolidation before breakout requires emotional discipline. Younger trader ICT (20s) would have panicked; experienced ICT (40s+) waits calmly.
- **Pyramiding discipline:** Use limit orders to avoid emotional chasing; let the market fill you rather than force entries.
- **Accepting imperfection:** Even missing the low candle by one candle is acceptable; don't chase missed entries; adjust and continue.
- **Transparency on execution:** Recording with smiley face emoji overlay and slow-motion rendering to X proves real-time execution, countering "hindsight/market replay" criticism.
- **Fun and entertainment:** ICT emphasizes this is not purely mechanical; humor and entertainment are essential for sustaining long-term trading interest.
- **Timestamps for psychology:** [0:26:19](https://youtu.be/SUcRywSry5U?t=1579) "Seek and destroy are very very attention demanding," [0:27:08](https://youtu.be/SUcRywSry5U?t=1628) "I would lose my mind... as a younger man," [0:32:55](https://youtu.be/SUcRywSry5U?t=1975) "I'm a little perturbed with myself," [0:28:42](https://youtu.be/SUcRywSry5U?t=1722) "I'm having fun. That's essential."
L26-023-P8Pn8DHFSW8

- **Chart management:** Use separate workspaces for different gap types (new week gaps, ORG, etc.) to avoid clutter. Only mark salient levels relevant to current price bias. A clean chart lets you focus on candle-by-candle tape reading (how bodies and wicks form).
- **Live trading on 1-minute:** Faster timeframe (15 seconds) is harder but proves you know what you're doing. 1m doesn't allow replaying—must analyze and act instantly.
- **Entries and fills:** Don't copy the trader directly. Learn the logic, find your own setups, use position sizing and stops that fit your account. Chasing the same entries at the same price (especially with 10,000 other people) means you don't get filled—someone else does.
- **Risk management:** Don't overlever. A micro contract (or even 1 contract) pulling 15–20 handles a couple times per week can cover monthly groceries. Build confidence slowly; don't rush to larger size.
- **The danger of self-doubt:** ICT notes he sometimes overthinks exits, second-guessing himself after feeling "led" to put a limit order at a specific level. He frames this as the conflict between experience/faith and flesh. Traders will experience the same—learn to trust your logic and rules; emotional second-guessing costs money.
- **Mindset on criticism:** ICT spends significant time defending his methodology against claims of rebranding or fraud. His argument: the logic works repeatedly, executions prove it, and critics offer no counter-demonstrations. His advice: ignore trolls; study the concepts, backtest, and verify yourself over 4 weeks.
- **Journaling:** Keep key levels on a notepad even if not all are drawn (avoids chart clutter but ensures you remember the backdrop).
L26-025-ieJSy4YsVgk

- **Regret and learning:** ICT openly expresses regret at not taking partials when planned. He notes this is his "gnawing little twist in your side" moment—the cost of learning session-type differences. The point: the structure is there, the opportunity is clear in hindsight, but execution in real-time is harder. New traders will feel the same.
- **Seat time in different sessions:** To master consolidation trades, you must spend time in them. You learn by *not* getting every tick but getting the pattern repeated.
- **Stopping out vs. exiting with profit:** ICT closes the position at 7530 (some profit after commissions) and ends the segment rather than holding till 9:30. He's avoiding overexposure into a binary event (Jackson Hole, summer doldrums). Risk management > greed.
- **Personal limits:** He notes back pain from sitting; he steps away despite the trade still having potential. Real traders have life constraints; know when to walk away.
L26-026-grcLMbjs-zs

- He will be low-output the following week; viewers should catch up on the last couple of months' videos ([0:24:11](https://youtu.be/grcLMbjs-zs?t=1451)).
L26-027-4KW2acdPi-M

- "How not to be surprised by the market": the quiet, choppy session precedes the big move, so don't switch off or lose focus ([0:14:23](https://youtu.be/4KW2acdPi-M?t=863)).
- Casual listeners miss the free, public rules (7–9, premium/discount); watch the lecture videos and the trader round-ups ([0:03:15](https://youtu.be/4KW2acdPi-M?t=195)).
- Live vs replay credibility segment ([0:24:39](https://youtu.be/4KW2acdPi-M?t=1479) to the end): when recording executions his screen shows the live market-open countdown (upper left), a countdown to candle close on the price axis, no replay toolbar; replay mode shows blue controls, a different banner, and candles that complete at once. He posts screenshots to a tweet thread while the video renders, and offers a $1M challenge to anyone who can fake it. This is mainly credibility material, not a trading lesson.
